sources.entry: copyparty - Portable file server with accelerated resumable uploads, deduplication, WebDAV, FTP, zeroconf, media indexer, video thumbnails, audio transcoding, and write-only folders, in a single file with no mandatory dependencies. (Demo) MIT Python
copyparty | Portable file server with resumable uploads, dedup, WebDAV and media indexing

summary.one_liner: copyparty is a portable Python file server that serves files over web browsers, WebDAV, SFTP, FTP, TFTP and SMB, with resumable uploads, deduplication and a media indexer, distributed as a single file.
summary.what_it_does: The server runs on Python 2 or 3 with all dependencies optional, and is started from a self-extracting copyparty-sfx.py file, a zipapp, a pip package, or a Windows exe. It serves files over HTTP(S), WebDAV, SFTP, FTP(S), TFTP and SMB/CIFS, with a browser UI supporting resumable multithreaded uploads, drag-and-drop, and folder downloads as zip or tar. Accounts and per-folder volumes control read, write, move, delete and admin permissions, and config can be set by arguments or config files. Optional extras add thumbnails via Pillow, pyvips or FFmpeg, audio and video handling, file and tag indexing and search, and upload deduplication via symlinks. The README also covers zeroconf/mDNS/SSDP announcements, event hooks, reverse-proxy and real-IP setup, and a markdown viewer and editor.
use_cases: share files from a home machine or NAS through a browser
accept large or resumable uploads from users with no client software
serve files over WebDAV or SFTP from an existing folder
run a quick temporary FTP or TFTP server for transferring files between machines
index and search music and files by tags, size, or date on a media share
set up per-user read-only or write-only drop folders
stack: FFmpeg (optional, thumbnails, audio transcoding, media tags)
notable: Single-file distribution: the sfx self-extractor, zipapp, or exe need no mandatory dependencies
Resumable, multithreaded browser uploads with 'race the beam' downloads while files are still uploading
Protocol coverage in one program: HTTP(S), WebDAV, SFTP, FTP(S), TFTP and SMB
Unpost (undo accidental uploads), self-destructing uploads, and write-only folders
Per-folder volumes with fine-grained permission letters and filekeys for unguessable links
caveats: SMB support is described by the README as unsafe, slow, and not recommended over WAN
Thumbnails for HEIC/HEIF and HEVC video are not available in the docker image or bootable flashdrive for legal reasons
Several bugs are listed, including issues with network-share databases, VirtualBox shared folders, and iOS audio playback
keywords: access files on my home server
